translationRepairs: The Duke of Zhou then said, "In the time of Tang there was yiyin, who relied upon August Heaven;
The Duke of Zhou then said, "In the time of Tang there was Yi Yin, who relied upon August Heaven;
Lowercase 'yiyin' is a clear spelling error for the personal name Yi Yin (伊尹).
The Duke of Zhou then said: "In Tang's time there was yiyin, who relied on the August Heaven;
The Duke of Zhou then said: "In Tang's time there was Yi Yin, who relied on the August Heaven;
Lowercase 'yiyin' is a clear spelling error for the personal name Yi Yin (伊尹).
In Zu Yi’s time there was Wu Xian;
In Zu Yi’s time there was Wu Hsien;
Chinese 巫賢 is a different person from 巫咸 (Wu Xian) in the previous sentence; English wrongly uses the same spelling for both.
In Zu Yi's time, there was Wu Xian;
In Zu Yi's time, there was Wu Hsien;
Chinese 巫賢 is a different person from 巫咸 (Wu Xian) in the previous sentence; English wrongly uses the same spelling for both.

The Yan ruler escorted Duke Huan of Qi out of the border. Duke Huan then ceded to Yan the territory he had taken, making Yan jointly pay tribute to the Son of Heaven, as in the duty during the time of Chengzhou;

The Yan ruler escorted Duke Huan of Qi out of the border. Duke Huan then ceded to Yan the territory to which Yan had come, making Yan jointly pay tribute to the Son of Heaven, as in the duty during the time of Chengzhou;
Chinese 燕所至地 means the lands as far as Yan (the escort) had reached, not territory Duke Huan 'had taken'.
General Shi Bei and the common people counterattacked the heir apparent Ping. He was killed, and his body was displayed as a warning.
General Shi Bei and the common people counterattacked the heir apparent Ping. General Shi Bei died and was displayed as a warning.
Chinese 將軍市被死，以徇 makes Shi Bei the one who died and was displayed; idiomatic 'He was killed' wrongly suggests Ping.
King Yi succeeded for twelve years and died. His son Yan Kuai succeeded.
King Yi reigned for twelve years and died. His son Yan Kuai succeeded.
立十二年 means he was on the throne twelve years; 'succeeded for twelve years' mistranslates the reign length.
Guo Kui said: "If the king must wish to attract scholars, start with Kui first.
Guo Kui said: "If the king truly wishes to attract scholars, start with Kui first.
必欲 means the king truly/certainly wishes to attract scholars; 'must wish' wrongly implies obligation.
Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard-pressed by Qin, and that Lian Po had left, so they made Pang Nuan the general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard-pressed by Qin, that Lian Po had left, and that Pang Nuan had been made general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
In 令龐煖將也 Yan observes that Zhao made Pang Nuan general; idiomatic 'they made' wrongly makes Yan the appointer.
Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard pressed by Qin, and Lian Po had left, so they made Pang Nuan general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard pressed by Qin, and Lian Po had left, and that Pang Nuan had been made general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
Same referent error: 令龐煖將也 is Zhao appointing Pang Nuan, not Yan.
